Harbhajan felt India should not have settled for a draw with New Zealand with 15 overs left. | Photo Credit: PTI
Harbhajan Singh has urged the International Cricket Council and the respective cricket Boards to rein in player behaviour after recent skirmishes between India and Pakistan at the under-19 and A levels.
Reacting to the exchanges during India-A’s defeat to Pakistan-A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars in Doha on Sunday and under-19 Asia Cup final, Harbhajan felt that it set a bad example for youngsters.
“Somewhere down the line, the ICC and the Boards need to step in. It’s getting a bit too much. The reactions of both Pakistan and Indian players after winning, and what happened, are not right.
“You should treat sports as sports. Heated moments are part of the sport, but it should not reach such a point where it feels shameful,” Harbhajan said at the launch of the HSBC Golf League.
“The ICC and the Boards should put their foot down and say, ‘this is not done’. Put all efforts on the field to win a game, but behaving in such a manner after the game is not right.”
India-A captain Tilak Varma and Pakistan-A skipper Abdul Samad skipped a handshake at the toss, with confusion over the result. Tensions escalated during Pakistan-A’s innings, with Harshit Rana exchanging words with Shamyl Hussain and Maaz Sadaqat.
Harbhajan also questioned India’s decision to settle for a draw in the Wellington Test against New Zealand with 15 overs left. “I would have bowled those 15 overs. Anil Kumble’s approach was always to fight till the last ball. I remember Michael Clarke taking two wickets in the last two overs in Sydney. You never know what can happen in those 15 overs”.
